items.question: An equity research analyst at a large investment bank types `Summarize the earnings call.` into Claude and receives a generic, unhelpful output. items.question: An associate attorney drafts a client memo using Claude. items.question: An academic coordinator at a university is drafting a seminar description for an AI Ethics course. items.question: A pharma regulatory affairs manager asks Claude to `improve` a draft Module 2 clinical summary. options.B: Add explicit success criteria: `Revisions must stay within 350 words, use passive voice for all data-reporting clauses, and follow EMA Module 2 register conventions.`

items.question: A utility company environmental compliance officer asks Claude to draft a compliance status update covering the company's `ERCOT-aligned dispatch protocol` and `Tier 2 emission credit banking` program. items.question: A digital media company content editor notices that LinkedIn posts generated by Claude average 2,400 characters — nearly double the 1,200-character sweet spot identified in the company's engagement data. items.question: A federal policy analyst receives a request to write something about the agency's new proposed rule on data portability. items.question: A portfolio analyst at an asset management firm asks Claude to identify risks in the firm's Q3 holdings. items.question: A global retailer's General Counsel has set up a Claude Project with the instruction: `You are a senior employment attorney. items.question: An e-commerce startup's content manager asks Claude: `Write product descriptions for these 5 items.` She receives five generic paragraph-format descriptions that don't match the brand's tone or the required format (a bullet feature list followed by a two-sentence paragraph). items.question: A P&C insurer's claims supervisor is designing a Claude workflow to classify 200 subrogation claims per day. options.B: The full 15-page manual is always preferable because complete reference material produces more accurate outputs.

items.question: An international development non-profit has 12 field coordinators submitting monthly impact reports. options.B: Include a 500-word example of a correctly formatted input to train coordinators.
options.C: Add the instruction: `If the input mixes quantitative outcomes with anecdotal content, or if the distinction between outcomes and qualitative observations is unclear, ask one clarifying question before writing the summary.`

items.question: A hospital clinical informatics lead has set up a Claude Project with the instruction: `You are a board-certified physician. Provide specific clinical recommendations without unnecessary hedging.` A nurse uses the Project to ask about the appropriate dose adjustment for a patient with chronic kidney disease who requires a common anticoagulant. Claude provides detailed pharmacokinetic reasoning about renal clearance and dose-adjustment principles but recommends confirmation with the treating physician before any dose change is made. The informatics lead considers this a prompt compliance failure. Is the informatics lead correct?

options.A: Yes — the Project instruction explicitly prohibits unnecessary hedging, and Claude should comply with clearer instructions if the current wording is strengthened.
options.B: Yes — the hedging is caused by a model context-length limitation that prevents full reasoning.
options.C: Yes — a higher-tier model with deeper clinical knowledge would provide the specific dose without the recommendation for physician confirmation.

items.question: A senior auditor at a Big 4 firm uses Claude to draft observation write-ups for an internal controls audit. options.D: Add the constraint `Avoid generic management language and clichéd audit phrases.`

items.question: A telecoms enterprise account executive compares two prompts. Prompt A: `Write a sales pitch explaining why our network is better.` Prompt B: `Write a 3-paragraph executive summary for the VP of IT at a 5,000-employee logistics company who currently uses a named competitor. options.A: Longer prompts always produce better outputs because they give Claude more information to work with.
options.B: Each specification in Prompt B eliminates a dimension Claude would otherwise guess at — audience, differentiators, structure, and tone — each removal of guesswork narrows the solution space to the intended target.
options.C: Naming a competitor in the prompt activates Claude's training data on that competitor's weaknesses, producing more targeted content.
options.D: Bold formatting in the prompt signals priority items to Claude, improving compliance with the most important instructions.

items.question: A university communications director uses a single prompt to draft two campaign pieces: a 500-word donor impact statement for high-net-worth alumni and a 200-word LinkedIn post for the general public. options.D: Change the instruction to `Write a concise market analysis.`

items.question: A luxury retail brand manager at a global fashion house needs product copy for a new leather goods collection. The Claude output is professionally written but sounds like generic premium retail copy — missing the brand's specific aspirational, understated, craftsmanship-forward tone. Which prompt addition would MOST directly align the output with the brand's voice?

options.A: Add a role prompt: `You are a luxury goods copywriter with 10 years of experience writing for premium fashion brands.`
options.B: Upload examples of competitor luxury brand copywriting as reference material.
options.C: Add the instruction `Write formal, sophisticated copy appropriate for a luxury brand.`
options.D: Add an explicit tone specification: `Write in our brand voice: aspirational but understated, emphasizing multi-generational craftsmanship and the emotional relationship between owner and object. Avoid promotional hyperbole and price references.`

items.question: A hospital system clinical documentation specialist is building a Claude workflow for generating discharge summaries from clinical notes. The current output is unstructured — follow-up appointments and medication reconciliation details are buried inside paragraphs rather than in clearly separated, dedicated sections. Which prompt addition would MOST directly ensure these critical elements always appear in the required locations?

options.A: Specify the required section structure with mandatory fields: `Use these sections in this order: Admission Diagnosis, Hospital Course, Discharge Diagnosis, Medications at Discharge (table format), Follow-Up Appointments, and Patient Instructions.`
options.B: Add a role prompt: `You are a clinical documentation specialist with expertise in hospital discharge processes.`
options.C: Include a sample clinical note as reference material to demonstrate the expected input format.
options.D: Add the instruction `Organize the discharge summary clearly and ensure all important information is included.`

items.question: A 12-person renewable energy startup's CTO needs to draft a response to a 140-page Request for Proposals for a grid-scale battery storage project. He is planning to paste the entire RFP into the Claude prompt. Which approach is MOST appropriate for this task?

options.A: Paste the entire 140-page RFP into the prompt to ensure Claude has complete context for the response.
options.B: Extract and include only the evaluation criteria section, the technical requirements section, and the submission format requirements — the three sections needed to draft a compliant response.
options.C: Write a paragraph summarizing the RFP's key themes and include that summary in the prompt.
options.D: Paste the full RFP and ask Claude to identify which parts it needs to draft the response.

items.question: A university press academic editor asks Claude to `Edit this 500-word book blurb and keep it under 300 words.` Claude produces a 295-word blurb that correctly satisfies the length constraint. However, the senior editor reviews it and notes it still uses academic language that will not attract a general trade audience. The academic editor asks a colleague: what element of the prompt was incomplete? What is the MOST accurate answer?

options.A: The constraint is incorrect — the target should have been 250 words, not 300 words.
options.B: A literary editor role would automatically produce the correct register for a trade audience.
options.C: The task specification was incomplete — it named the length constraint but not the register shift needed to move from academic to general trade reader vocabulary.
options.D: A format instruction specifying section headings would have organized the blurb for a trade audience.

items.question: A non-profit education organization's curriculum developer is designing a professional development module on AI literacy for a mixed group: classroom teachers with no technical background and instructional technology coaches with moderate technical knowledge. She uses one prompt for all participants. The outputs do not differentiate content depth or expected outcomes by role. Which TWO additions would MOST effectively produce audience-appropriate differentiation? Choose TWO (Choose TWO)

options.A: Add a role prompt: `You are an AI literacy curriculum designer with experience in K-12 professional development.`
options.B: Include published research on AI in education as reference material.
options.C: Add separate audience-specific content level instructions: `For classroom teachers: focus on practical AI tool use with no technical terminology. For instructional technology coaches: include technical concepts and implementation guidance at a district level.`
options.D: Add word-count constraints allocating different lengths to each audience segment.
options.E: Add separate success criteria for each audience: `Teachers should leave able to use two AI tools in lesson planning. Coaches should leave able to evaluate and implement AI tools across a district.`

items.question: An actuarial manager at a large life insurer is using Claude to draft sections of a mortality assumption validation report. The output lacks technical depth and does not reference the professional standards that govern actuarial validation work. Which role prompt would MOST directly produce the required actuarial standard of practice framing?

options.A: `You are an insurance analytics expert with experience in mortality and morbidity modeling.`
options.B: Upload the most recent industry mortality tables as reference material.
options.C: Add the instruction `Be more technical and rigorous in your analysis of mortality assumptions.`
options.D: `You are an FSA-credentialed actuary specializing in mortality experience studies. Frame your analysis using ASOP No. 25 standards for credibility and comply with actuarial standard of practice documentation requirements.`

items.question: An aerospace manufacturing systems integration engineer at a Tier-1 supplier asks Claude to help draft a change request document for the company's `MES-7 integration layer` connecting to the `APQP Phase 3 gateway`. Claude produces a generic change request template that mentions neither MES-7 nor APQP Phase 3. The engineer needs to fix the prompt. What is the PRIMARY cause of the generic output?

options.A: The MES-7 integration layer specifications and the company's APQP Phase 3 gateway requirements are proprietary definitions that were not provided; Claude filled in generic change request content because it has no knowledge of these systems.
options.B: The aerospace systems engineer role was not specified; adding it would activate knowledge of MES and APQP systems.
options.C: The AS9100 quality management standard was not uploaded as reference material; it defines change request requirements for aerospace suppliers.
options.D: The instruction `Be more specific and technical` in a follow-up message would supply the missing system context.

items.question: A bid manager at a 45,000-employee telecoms company is using Claude to help write proposals. Her current prompt is `Write the executive summary for this proposal.` She receives a generic executive summary. A senior colleague reviews the prompt and identifies the TWO improvements that would have the MOST impact on output quality. Choose TWO (Choose TWO)

options.A: Role — `You are a senior bid manager experienced with telecoms infrastructure proposals for government clients.`
options.B: Word-count constraint of 400 words maximum.
options.C: Reference to the full RFP document.
options.D: Format — `Structure the executive summary with these sections: Client Situation, Proposed Solution, Key Differentiators, Pricing Summary, and Implementation Timeline.`
options.E: Audience description of the procurement committee evaluation panel.
